title: MR Imaging and Radiomics Features for Predicting Variant Histology of Bladder Cancer: A Single Centre Retrospective Analysis.
abstract: Introduction Compare MRI features of bladder variant histology (VH) and pure urothelial carcinoma (UC) and determine if MRI radiomics features can predict VH. Methods In this retrospective study, cystectomy pathology database search yielded 37 patients with tumours with more than 50% VH and preoperative MRI's. Cystectomy database search yielded 38 consecutive patients with pure UC and preoperative MRI's. Three radiologists characterized MRI T2, diffusion-weighted, apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) maps and postcontrast features of bladder tumours. Inter-reader agreement was assessed using Gwet's agreement and intra-class coefficients. Another radiologist segmented bladder tumours and adjacent perivesical fat on T2-weighted and ADC images using radiomics software. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) was used to determine radiomics features that distinguished VH from UC. Fifty datasets were prepared using multiple imputation approach, and variables were normalized for LASSO variable selection. Results Patients with VH (mean age = 68, 54 (72%) men) included squamous cell (n = 17), sarcomatoid (n = 6), plasmacytoid (n = 6), adenocarcinoma (n = 4) and small cell (n = 4) variants. Inter-reader agreement was similar for VH and UC (p > 0.44). All readers characterized all squamous cell carcinoma as T2 intermediate. For two of three readers, 92%-100% of hypoenhancing tumours were VH at pathology whereas 74%-78% of hyperenhancing masses were UC (p = 0.001). Combination of 11 selected radiomics features had AUC of 0.98 for training and 0.95 for validation data for prediction of VH. Conclusion Squamous cell carcinoma was T2 intermediate, and VH was more likely to hypoenhance compared to UC. Our radiomic model had excellent performance for predicting VH.

title: Radiation therapy for persistent or progressive mediastinal lymphoma after chemotherapy in FeLV-positive cats: a retrospective case series of four cats.
abstract: Background Mediastinal lymphoma in feline leukaemia virus (FeLV)-positive cats is associated with a poor prognosis, and therapeutic options may be limited when adequate disease control is not achieved with chemotherapy. The efficacy of radiation therapy in this setting has not been established. Case report Medical records were retrospectively reviewed for FeLV-positive cats diagnosed with mediastinal lymphoma between November 2018 and December 2024 that had persistent or progressive mediastinal disease after chemotherapy and were subsequently treated with radiation therapy. Treatment response was assessed by computed tomography using the Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumours (RECIST). Three of four cats (75%) responded to radiation therapy (two complete responses, one partial response). Respiratory signs improved rapidly in three cats (median 5 days). Local disease control was achieved in most cases; however, three cats developed progression at other sites. Survival times were 45, 150 and 352 days in cats that died, and one cat remained alive for >626 days at the time of last follow-up. No severe radiation-related adverse effects were documented during the available follow-up, although systematic evaluation of late radiation toxicity was not possible. Conclusion Radiation therapy may provide local control and rapid palliation of respiratory signs in FeLV-positive cats with persistent or progressive mediastinal lymphoma after chemotherapy. Further studies with larger cohorts are warranted.

title: Cytomorphologic Features of Hepatic PEComa Diagnosed by Fine-Needle Aspiration Biopsy.
abstract: Perivascular epithelioid cell tumours (PEComas) are rare mesenchymal neoplasms with characteristic myomelanocytic differentiation and limited descriptions in fine-needle aspiration (FNA) specimens. A woman in her 30s with a history of ALK-positive anaplastic large cell lymphoma in remission was found to have a 2.1-cm hepatic mass during evaluation of persistent liver function abnormalities. Ultrasound-guided FNA demonstrated a cellular neoplasm composed of loosely cohesive clusters and singly dispersed epithelioid to spindle cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm, mild to moderate nuclear atypia and prominent nucleoli. Immunohistochemical studies showed positivity for smooth muscle actin, caldesmon, HMB-45 and Melan-A, supporting a myomelanocytic phenotype. Molecular testing identified pathogenic TSC2 splice-site mutations. Subsequent resection confirmed hepatic PEComa, epithelioid angiomyolipoma variant. This case highlights the characteristic cytomorphologic, immunophenotypic and molecular features of hepatic PEComa and demonstrates the value of FNA with ancillary testing in establishing a preoperative diagnosis and excluding morphologic mimics.

title: Unravelling A Rare Diagnosis: Pulmonary Alveolar Proteinosis.
abstract: Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (PAP) is a rare disorder characterized by abnormal accumulation of surfactant within the alveoli, leading to impaired gas exchange and progressive respiratory symptoms. We report a 40-year-old stone grinder presenting with chronic cough, dyspnea, weight loss and hypoxemia. High-resolution computed tomography showed bilateral ground-glass opacities, while bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) yielded characteristic milky fluid. Cytological examination demonstrated PAS-positive eosinophilic material with foamy macrophages, confirming secondary PAP related to silica exposure. Lung biopsy was not feasible because of the patient's condition. Whole lung lavage resulted in marked clinical, radiological and oxygenation improvement, highlighting BAL cytology's diagnostic value.

title: Internal Validation of a YOLOv8 Model for Classifying Temporomandibular Joint Disc Displacement With Versus Without Reduction on Open-Mouth Proton-Density-Weighted MRI.
abstract: Background The temporomandibular joint (TMJ) disc plays an important role in maintaining normal joint function. However, disc displacement is a common condition that can lead to pain, restricted jaw movement and chronic TMJ dysfunction. Objective To develop and evaluate a deep learning model capable of autonomously localizing the TMJ region from magnetic resonance (MR) images during mouth opening using the You Only Look Once (YOLO) v8 framework, and to discriminate between TMJ disc displacement with reduction (DDwR) and disc displacement without reduction (DDwoR). Methods This study included 237 patients (48 males, 189 females; age range, 19-83 [mean, 44.73 ± 18.3] years) who underwent MRI examination at our hospital for suspected TMJ disorders and were diagnosed with disc displacement based on imaging findings. After exclusion, 439 proton density-weighted MR images during mouth opening were preprocessed and divided on a patient basis into training (280 images), validation (71 images) and test (88 images) datasets. The TMJ region was manually annotated using LabelImg, including the condyles, articular disc and articular tubercle. The YOLOv8 deep learning model was trained for 200 epochs to localize the TMJ region and classify DDwR or DDwoR. Results The YOLOv8 model achieved promising results for the detection and classification of TMJ disc displacements. The performance metrics were a precision, recall and F1 score of 0.983, 0.988 and 0.987, respectively, indicating a high accuracy in detecting and identifying disc displacement patterns. Conclusion The YOLOv8 deep learning model demonstrated promising performance in automatically localizing and classifying TMJ disc displacement from MR images.

title: Benchmarking deep learning-based reconstruction methods for photoacoustic computed tomography with clinically relevant synthetic datasets.
abstract: Significance Deep learning (DL)-based image reconstruction methods for photoacoustic computed tomography (PACT) have developed rapidly in recent years. However, most existing methods have not employed standardized datasets, and their evaluations rely on traditional image quality (IQ) metrics that may lack clinical relevance. The absence of a standardized framework for clinically meaningful IQ assessment hinders fair comparison and raises concerns about the reproducibility and reliability of reported advancements in PACT. Aim A benchmarking framework is proposed that provides open-source, anatomically plausible synthetic datasets and evaluation strategies for DL-based acoustic inversion methods in PACT. Approach The datasets each include over 10,000 two-dimensional (2D) stochastic breast objects with clinically relevant lesions and paired measurements at varying modeling complexity. The evaluation strategies incorporate both traditional and task-based IQ measures to assess fidelity and clinical utility. A preliminary benchmarking study is conducted to demonstrate the framework's utility by comparing DL-based and physics-based reconstruction methods. Results The benchmarking study demonstrated that the proposed framework enabled comprehensive, quantitative comparisons of reconstruction performance and revealed important limitations in certain DL-based methods. Although they performed well according to traditional IQ measures, they often failed to accurately recover lesions. This highlights the inadequacy of traditional metrics and motivates the need for task-based assessments. Conclusions The proposed benchmarking framework enables systematic comparisons of DL-based acoustic inversion methods for 2D PACT. By integrating clinically relevant synthetic datasets with rigorous evaluation protocols, it enables reproducible, objective assessments and facilitates method development and system optimization in PACT.

title: Ultrasound-driven electronically programmable microbubbles.
abstract: Ultrasound-actuated microbubbles have served as efficient microscale engines demonstrating wireless actuation, simplified robotic architectures, and rapid response. Despite recent advances, a limitation of many microbubble technologies is that they use passive capturing of bubbles. The lack of control over bubble placement and size hinders the ability to individually address specified bubbles, a feature that would be important for performing multiple functions. Here, we present an on-chip bubble customization platform that enables active control of individual microbubbles. Instead of trapping bubbles, we purposely generate them via electrolysis on electrode arrays. The bubbles, when actuated by an external ultrasound input, create a variety of programmed flows ranging from streaming due to volumetric oscillation of a single bubble to diverse symmetry-broken directional flows when multiple bubbles interact. The bubble configuration can also be altered by simply increasing the electrolysis voltage on specified electrodes to detach the unneeded bubbles. We find that in this regime, when coupled to acoustic oscillations, we can generate a distinct bubble shooting flow pattern whose flow direction is selectively controlled by the incident ultrasound frequency. Collectively, the active bubble reconfiguration ability unlocks a range of previously inaccessible acoustofluidic functions in a single device with unprecedented controllability.

We find that in this regime, when coupled to acoustic oscillations, we can generate a distinct bubble shooting flow pattern whose flow direction is selectively controlled by the incident ultrasound frequency. Collectively, the active bubble reconfiguration ability unlocks a range of previously inaccessible acoustofluidic functions in a single device with unprecedented controllability.

title: Recurrent Intermittent Small Bowel Obstruction as an Initial Manifestation of Primary Intestinal Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma: A Case Report and Systematic Literature Review.
abstract: Primary intestinal diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is a rare gastrointestinal malignancy and an uncommon cause of small bowel obstruction (SBO). We report a 70-year-old man with no history of abdominal surgery who presented with recurrent episodes of abdominal pain, vomiting, and transiently resolving SBO. Serial computed tomography (CT) demonstrated a persistent transition point associated with an increasingly evident mesenteric soft tissue mass, initially suspected to represent a neuroendocrine tumor. After repeated presentations and temporary improvement with conservative management, exploratory laparotomy revealed a distal ileal tumor with central mesenteric involvement encasing major mesenteric vessels. Segmental small bowel resection with primary anastomosis was performed, although macroscopic mesenteric disease remained. Histopathological examination confirmed CD10-positive DLBCL, and systemic treatment with six cycles of R-CHOP was initiated. A structured search of MEDLINE and Embase identified 78 publications describing 87 adult cases of intestinal lymphoma presenting with SBO. DLBCL was the most frequently reported subtype, and the ileum was the most commonly specified anatomical location. However, recurrent obstruction with transient clinical and radiological improvement was rarely emphasized. This case demonstrates that temporary resolution of obstructive symptoms does not exclude a persistent pathological lead point. Recurrent SBO in a patient without previous abdominal surgery, particularly when serial imaging demonstrates evolving mesenteric or intestinal abnormalities, should prompt renewed investigation for an underlying malignancy, including intestinal lymphoma. Repeat cross-sectional imaging, multidisciplinary reassessment, and individualized consideration of operative exploration may facilitate timely diagnosis while avoiding conclusions that transient improvement represents definitive resolution.

title: The Prevalence of Histologically Confirmed Endometriosis in Salpingectomy Specimens for Hydrosalpinx and Subsequent Reproductive Outcomes.
abstract: Background Hydrosalpinx, a fluid-filled blocked fallopian tube, is a major cause of infertility and is mainly linked to pelvic inflammatory disease. However, its connection to endometriosis, especially hidden tubal endometriosis without visible signs, is not well studied. This research aimed to find the prevalence of confirmed endometriosis in salpingectomy samples removed due to hydrosalpinx and to evaluate the subsequent reproductive outcomes. Methods A cross-sectional study involved 70 infertile women undergoing laparoscopic salpingectomy at a specialized center. We gathered demographic, surgical, and pathological information from medical records. The main outcome was the occurrence of endometriosis based on histopathology. The secondary outcome was the rate of clinical pregnancies (either spontaneous or through ART) after salpingectomy. We used SPSS v23.0 for statistical analysis, considering p < 0.05 as significant. Results The average age of participants was 37.38 ± 6.13 years. Clear histological evidence of endometriosis was found in 14.3% (10/70) of samples. Notably, 8% (4/50) of patients without a history of endometriosis had hidden tubal disease. The visual detection of endometriosis during laparoscopy was marginally significantly associated with a positive pathology (37.5% vs. 7.4%, p = 0.050). After salpingectomy, the total clinical pregnancy rate was 25.5% (12/47). However, none of the patients (0%) with a diagnosis of tubal endometriosis achieved pregnancy, while those with other pathologies had a 30% success rate. Conclusion Examining salpingectomy samples is essential for detecting endometriosis. Women with histologically confirmed tubal endometriosis may represent a subgroup with potentially poorer reproductive outcomes. However, this observation is exploratory and requires validation in larger studies with adequate adjustment for age, ovarian reserve, and ART-related factors.

title: Local RAGE Inhibition Attenuates Early Diabetic Retinal Pathology in Streptozotocin-Induced Rats.
abstract: Introduction Diabetic retinopathy, which occurs during extended periods of chronic hyperglycemia, is one of the main causes of vision loss. The receptor for advanced glycation end products (RAGE) plays a central role in inflammatory and angiogenic signaling, both of which contribute to the pathogenesis of diabetic retinopathy, but its therapeutic targeting in ocular disease has been insufficiently explored. Methods We evaluated topical RAGE229, a small-molecule RAGE inhibitor, and an intravitreally administered anti-RAGE antibody in a streptozotocin-induced diabetic rat model. At day 84, treatment effects were assessed using masked fundoscopic scoring, RT-qPCR, immunohistochemistry, and histological morphometry. Treated eyes were evaluated against both route-matched diabetic vehicle-control groups and paired contralateral vehicle-treated eyes. Results Both interventions reduced fundoscopic pathology and retinal Vegfa and Nfkb1 expression, whereas Ager showed only a non-significant downward trend. NF-κB p65 immunoreactivity was reduced by both treatments, while a significant reduction in VEGF-A immunoreactivity was detected only in the paired anti-RAGE antibody analysis. Morphometric analysis indicated attenuation of diabetes-associated retinal thinning with both interventions. Neither intervention altered systemic glycemic control. Although both interventions demonstrated similar overall anatomical protection, anti-RAGE antibody treatment showed more consistent effects across protein-level and structural endpoints. Conclusion These findings provide proof-of-concept evidence that local RAGE-targeted treatment may attenuate vascular, molecular, and structural manifestations of early experimental diabetic retinopathy without detectable changes in systemic glycemia. Further preclinical studies should evaluate ocular exposure, direct target engagement, functional visual outcomes, and reproducibility in larger cohorts.

title: Use of Myocardial Perfusion Imaging to Guide Prognosis and Management in Older Adults: Is There an Age Limit?
abstract: Background Myocardial perfusion imaging is used to guide risk stratification and revascularization decisions. We aimed to determine whether the prognostic value of ischemia on myocardial perfusion imaging and the association with early revascularization (ER) and outcomes differ across age groups. Methods We included 73 038 patients who underwent single photon emission computed tomography (n=45 252) or positron emission tomography (n=27 786) myocardial perfusion imaging across 20 sites from 2009 to 2024. ER was defined as revascularization within 90 days post-myocardial perfusion imaging. Propensity score-adjusted Cox models evaluated the interaction between age, ischemic burden (myocardial flow reserve for positron emission tomography), and ER for the primary outcome of all-cause death or nonfatal myocardial infarction. Results Median age was 66 years; 45.3% were <65, 31.5% were 65 to 74, 19.1% were 75 to 84, and 4.2% were ≥85. ER was performed in 6.1%, rising to 7.0% in those aged 75 to 84 years and decreasing to 6.5% in those aged ≥85 years. During a median follow-up of 3.7 years, 10 757 deaths/myocardial infarctions occurred. Increasing ischemia was associated with lower event rates after ER versus medical therapy across most age groups, with no significant continuous age-ischemia-ER interaction ( P =0.748). In an exploratory analysis of 3031 patients aged ≥85 years, this association appeared attenuated (hazard ratio for ischemia >10%: 0.90 [0.64-1.26]), although precision was limited, likely reflecting, in part, the small number of patients undergoing ER (n=198). Among positron emission tomography patients, the myocardial flow reserve×ER association did not vary with age (3-way interaction P =0.689). In analyses excluding patients with ER, ischemia remained prognostic in all age groups, though its associated risk declined with advancing age. Conclusions Ischemia remains prognostic across all ages and may help identify candidates who have improved outcomes with ER. In an exploratory analysis, this association appeared attenuated in patients aged ≥85 years, a hypothesis-generating observation. Positron emission tomography-derived myocardial flow reserve may provide complementary physiological information for treatment selection in older adults.

title: Anatomical determinants of DTI-ALPS: Effects of ROI definition, ventricular morphology, and periventricular deformation.
abstract: The diffusion tensor image analysis along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS) index is increasingly used as a non-invasive MRI biomarker proposed to reflect glymphatic and perivascular function, yet the anatomical validity and measurement stability of the metric remain incompletely characterised. Using diffusion MRI data from 850 healthy young adults and 150 healthy ageing participants from the Human Connectome Project, I systematically evaluated the influence of region-of-interest (ROI) placement and ventricular anatomy on ALPS measurements. Reference ALPS implementations demonstrated substantial hemispheric variability, with a median left-right difference of 12.5% and marked asymmetry in the underlying numerator and denominator tensor components. A two-stage optimisation framework incorporating fibre-pool alignment, hemispheric symmetry, component stability, and directional purity identified anatomically improved ROI configurations that significantly increased fibre specificity and reduced measurement variability in independent validation cohorts. Despite these improvements, residual hemispheric asymmetry persisted, suggesting an intrinsic anatomical contribution to ALPS variability. In the healthy ageing cohort, ventricular volume emerged as the strongest predictor of ALPS, explaining substantially more variance than chronological age. Voxel-wise deformation-based morphometry demonstrated that lower ALPS values were associated with ventricular and periventricular expansion, while optimisation increased coupling between ALPS and ventricular anatomy. Collectively, these findings indicate that ALPS measurements are strongly influenced by ROI definition, ventricular morphology, and surrounding periventricular tissue architecture. Rather than functioning as a direct measure of glymphatic transport in isolation, ALPS appears to represent a composite anatomical diffusion biomarker shaped by both methodological implementation and underlying neuroanatomy. These results provide a framework for improving methodological standardisation and interpretation of ALPS measurements in future neuroimaging studies.

In the healthy ageing cohort, ventricular volume emerged as the strongest predictor of ALPS, explaining substantially more variance than chronological age. Voxel-wise deformation-based morphometry demonstrated that lower ALPS values were associated with ventricular and periventricular expansion, while optimisation increased coupling between ALPS and ventricular anatomy. Collectively, these findings indicate that ALPS measurements are strongly influenced by ROI definition, ventricular morphology, and surrounding periventricular tissue architecture. Rather than functioning as a direct measure of glymphatic transport in isolation, ALPS appears to represent a composite anatomical diffusion biomarker shaped by both methodological implementation and underlying neuroanatomy. These results provide a framework for improving methodological standardisation and interpretation of ALPS measurements in future neuroimaging studies.

title: Orbital Abscess Complicating Allergic Fungal Rhinosinusitis Due to Streptococcus halichoeri: A Rare Zoonotic Sinonasal Infection.
abstract: Background Secondary bacterial infections complicating allergic fungal rhinosinusitis (AFRS) are uncommon but can be serious given the expansile nature of the disease which can thin and erode the bone separating the sinuses from the brain and orbits. Zoonotic pathogens are rarely implicated as pathogens. Case report A 21-year-old African American male with several years of progressive nasal obstruction, facial pressure, and hyposmia, presented emergently with acute left eye pain and swelling, diplopia, afferent pupillary defect and inferior visual field deficit. Computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated acute on chronic sinusitis with a left orbital abscess. The patient underwent emergent endoscopic sinus surgery with left orbitotomy and drainage of the orbital abscess. Intraoperative findings, pathology, cultures, and allergy testing were reviewed demonstrating AFRS and a novel zoonotic bacterium, Streptococcus halichoeri . Conclusions This case represents the first otolaryngologic case of S. halichoeri infection, a severe and complicated sinus and orbital infection. It is unclear if the severity of this infection was a consequence of the unusual pathogen, of the long-term thinning of the bone around the orbit, or both. Although AFRS is not considered an infection, secondary bacterial infection may occur and cause severe complications. Early surgical intervention and culture-directed therapy are essential in managing complicated sinonasal diseases.

title: EXPRESS: Longitudinal Quantitative MRI of Blood-Brain Barrier Leakage in Chronic Cerebral Hypoperfusion Rat model.
abstract: Objective-Methods:Chronic cerebral-hypoperfusion is a key contributor to vascular cognitive impairment, with blood-brain barrier (BBB) dysfunction proposed as an early driver of white matter injury. The temporal-evolution and regional-heterogeneity of BBB-leakage remain poorly characterized in vivo. We longitudinally assessed BBB permeability in Sprague-Dawley rats subjected to bilateral-common carotid artery occlusion (2VO) versus sham controls using contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI 9.4T over 12-weeks. Gadolinium-leakage maps were generated and analyzed in predefined regions (cortex, hippocampus, striatum, corpus callosum). Exploratory histological observations included GFAP immunostaining, and circulating biochemical biomarkers (sTWEAK, MMP-9, GOT, cytokines) were quantified.Results:Localized BBB disruption was observed at weeks 3, 6 post-2VO and progressed heterogeneously, with pronounced leakage strictly targeted toward corpus callosum, hippocampus and striatum. Despite descriptive trends showing increased astroglial activation, systemic biochemical biomarkers did not correlate with imaging-derived central BBB-leakage. Volumetric analysis revealed subtle but significant brain atrophy (18% whole-brain reduction) preceding overt T2-signal abnormalities. In the 2VO model studied, BBB dysfunction in chronic-hypoperfusion appears to be a dynamic, region-specific process.Conclusion:Longitudinal contrast-enhanced MRI detected changes that were not mirrored by the circulating biomarkers studied, suggesting its potential utility as a surrogate endpoint in preclinical studies, which should be confirmed in larger cohorts and complementary models.

title: EXPRESS: Diagnostic and prognostic value of on-site CT-derived fractional flow reserve in intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis.
abstract: Background The role of CT-derived fractional flow reserve (CT-FFR) in cerebrovascular disease remains undefined. This study validated the diagnostic and prognostic value of an on-site CT-FFR in symptomatic intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis (sICAS) patients. Methods This retrospective study enrolled sICAS patients with 30 - 99% stenosis confirmed by CTA, divided into two substudies. The diagnostic performance study included 259 patients undergoing CTA and CT perfusion (CTP) or four-dimensional CTA (CTP as reference standard). In prognosis study, 452 patients with at least 1-year follow-up were included. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) model was used to measure CT-FFR. Diagnostic performance was assessed by receiver-operating characteristic (ROC) curves, and predictive value by Cox regression analysis. Results The diagnostic performance of CT-FFR was significantly higher than diameter stenosis (DS) on both per-patient (P = 0.009) and per-lesion (P = 0.004) basis. And the cut-off value of CT-FFR diagnosing cerebral hypoperfusion was 0.80. 15.0% (68 / 452) patients experienced recurrent ischemic events during the median 24 (17-33) months follow-up. CT-FFR provided incremental prognostic value beyond traditional cardiovascular risks plus DS (AUC = 0.797 vs 0.716, P < 0.001). Conclusion This on-site CT-FFR can serve as a valuable tool for diagnosis and risk stratification in sICAS patients.

title: Survivor bias and disease progression in observational cohorts in multiple sclerosis.
abstract: Background Long-term studies on multiple sclerosis progression often face dropout, possibly among those with more aggressive disease, biasing the cohort. Objectives We assessed potential survivorship bias in a long-term observational multiple sclerosis cohort. Methods Three hundred sixty-one patients with multiple sclerosis were followed for 10 years, with clinical assessments, blood biomarkers and magnetic resonance imaging at baseline, follow-up 1 and follow-up 2. Progression was defined as an Expanded Disability Status Scale increase. Dropout was analysed and predicted; estimated Expanded Disability Status Scale was calculated for dropouts to assess bias. Brain volumes were normalized. Results One hundred and sixty-two patients with multiple sclerosis completed all follow-ups; 81 showed progression. Dropout rates were 97/361 at follow-up 1 and 102/264 at follow-up 2. Dropouts had worse Expanded Disability Status Scale, Nine-Hole Peg test, Timed 25-Foot Walk, lower brain volume and higher lesion volume before dropping out. Blood biomarkers did not differ. Main dropout predictors were higher baseline Expanded Disability Status Scale, lesion volume, worse Nine-Hole Peg test and shorter disease duration. Median estimated Expanded Disability Status Scale at follow-up 2 for dropouts was 5.5 versus 3.5 for non-dropouts. Discussion Fewer than half completed the study. High lesion load and worse clinical status predicted dropout. This may cause underestimation of progression and reduced statistical power. Similar bias may affect other long-term studies in chronic diseases.

title: Routine versus postoperative CRP/CT guided selective diverting ileostomy after laparoscopic low anterior resection for rectal cancer: a comparative randomized controlled trial.
abstract: Background Diverting ileostomy is routinely used to protect the anastomosis after laparoscopic low anterior resection (LAR) for rectal cancer, but it exposes most patients to stoma-related morbidity even though only a minority develop a true anastomotic leak. This trial evaluated whether a postoperative C-reactive protein (CRP) and computed tomography (CT) guided selective ileostomy strategy could reduce the rate of ileostomy formation compared with routine diversion. Methods In this RCT, 200 patients with stage II or III middle or lower third rectal cancer undergoing laparoscopic LAR were randomized 1:1 to a CRP/CT-guided selective ileostomy group (n = 100) or a routine diverting ileostomy group (n = 100). In the CRP/CT group, serum CRP was measured daily from postoperative day 1; a threshold of 114 mg/L on day 3 or a rise greater than 15 mg/L per day triggered confirmatory contrast-enhanced CT, with ileostomy formed only if findings were suspicious for leak. The primary outcome was the stoma-free status throughout the 12-month follow-up. Results Baseline demographic and tumor characteristics were similar between groups (all p > 0.05). Ileostomy formation was markedly lower in the CRP/CT group than the routine group (22.0% vs. 100.0%, p < 0.001). Anastomotic leak rates did not differ (0% vs. 1.0%, p = 1.000), nor did overall complication rates (31.0% vs. 32.0%, p = 0.879). Operative time (148.4 ± 14.0 vs. 166.6 ± 13.1 min, p < 0.001) and intraoperative blood loss (168.9 ± 28.2 vs. 197.3 ± 39.7 mL, p < 0.001) were significantly lower in the CRP/CT group. Stoma-related complications were far less frequent with the selective strategy (3.0% vs. 30.0%, p < 0.001). The CRP/CT group reported significantly better global health status, physical functioning, and emotional functioning scores (all p < 0.001). Conclusion A postoperative CRP/CT-guided selective ileostomy strategy reduces the need for diverting ileostomy after laparoscopic low anterior resection for rectal cancer while improving operative outcomes and quality of life; however, confirmed leakage was infrequent in both groups. This approach may serve as an alternative to routine diversion in appropriately monitored surgical units. Trial registration This trial was retrospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (Identifier: NCT07722533) on July 17, 2026.

title: Estimation of glomerular filtration rate by standard renal CT imaging.
abstract: Objectives To develop and evaluate a method to predict glomerular filtration rate (GFR) from clinical renal CT. Materials and methods Medical records of adult living kidney donors operated between 2013 and 2022 and patients considered for neoadjuvant cisplatin prior to cystectomy between 2019 and 2024 were retrospectively reviewed. Inclusion criteria were (1) renal CT obtained at 100 or 120 kVp before and 5-15 min after contrast administration, and (2) iohexol clearance test within 2 months of imaging. The iohexol clearance test was performed on the same day as the cystatin C and creatinine measurements. Estimated GFR values included cystatin C-based eGFR (eGFR cystatin C ), creatinine-based eGFR using the Cockcroft-Gault formula (eGFR Cockcroft-Gault ), and eGFR using the Revised Lund-Malmö formula (eGFR LMR18 ), which is based on both creatinine and cystatin C. Manual and automatic segmentations of the renal pelvis and bladder were performed in both the excretory and unenhanced phases. Results In total, 139 patients were included in the analysis (mean age 52 ± 13 years; 60% women). Multivariate linear regression analysis combining the segmentation-derived variable with body surface area and age gave an adjusted R-square of 0.77 to mGFR iohexol (p < 0.001). title: Fluent but not fail-safe: machine-translated radiology reports still need expert review.
abstract: Objectives Cross-border care, teleradiology, and international referral pathways increasingly require radiology report translation, but isolated mistranslations may alter clinical meaning. We evaluated German-to-English machine translation of radiology reports and correction-based localization of text requiring review. Materials and methods In this retrospective study, 310 de-identified German radiology reports from June and July 2025 were translated into English with DeepL. Eight radiologists assigned 5-point quality scores and corrected perceived errors. Thirty reports were reviewed by all eight readers, and 280 reports were assigned for single-reader evaluation, yielding 520 evaluations. Automated metrics and large language model judges were tested for report-level identification of translations requiring review; a correction-based segment-level edit-prediction model was evaluated on held-out shared reports. Results Most translations were rated good or excellent (339/520, 65.2%), but clinically important mistranslations involved diagnosis, anatomy, and radiologic terminology. Agreement was low for ordinal quality scores (Krippendorff α = 0.078, p = 0.006) but high for expert corrections (pairwise "bilingual evaluation understudy"-BLEU = 83.0, p < 0.001). In the conservative primary screen of 30 shared reports, no automated method discriminated translations requiring review (area under receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC] = 0.51-0.65; p = 0.100-0.920). The final edit-prediction model achieved a concordance index of 0.697 and an AUC of 0.731 for segments edited by at least six of eight readers. Conclusion Machine-translated radiology reports were often acceptable on average, but translations containing errors requiring expert review persisted. Expert corrections were more reproducible than ordinal quality scores and supported localization of text requiring human review. Key points Question Cross-border radiology workflows increasingly require report translation, but fluent machine translations may still contain meaning-changing errors requiring expert review for safe care. Findings Most machine translations were rated good or excellent, yet clinically important mistranslations occurred, and automated report-level metrics did not reliably identify reports needing review. Relevance statement Machine translation may support cross-border radiology workflows, but clinically important mistranslations in otherwise fluent reports require human-in-the-loop oversight and tools that localize text requiring expert review.

title: Dose-Escalated Focal Salvage High-Dose-Rate Brachytherapy and Genomic Classifier Risk Stratification in Radiorecurrent Prostate Cancer: The F-SHARP Phase I/II Clinical Trial.
abstract: Purpose Prospective data on the management of intraprostatic radiorecurrence (IPR) after definitive radiotherapy (RT) and use of genomic classifiers (GC) in this setting are limited. We hypothesized that dose-escalated focal salvage high-dose-rate brachytherapy (DE-fsHDR) would be safe and effective, and that GC would risk stratify patients who may benefit from treatment intensification. Methods F-SHARP is a multi-institutional phase I/II trial of DE-fsHDR for IPR after any form of RT for localized prostate cancer. Patients received up to 30 Gy in 1-2 fractions. The primary objective was to determine the acute RT-related grade ≥3 CTCAE v4.03 genitourinary and GI toxicity rates. Secondary end points included all-grade toxicity, quality of life (QoL; EPIC-26 and International Prostate Symptom Score), disease control, and survival. GC analysis used a clinical-grade transcriptome assay (Veracyte, San Diego, CA). Time-to-event outcomes included biochemical progression-free survival (bPFS), radiographic progression-free survival (rPFS), local recurrence-free survival (LRFS), and metastasis-free survival (MFS). Results Twenty-four participants received one fraction and 38 received two fractions (N = 62). The median follow-up was 39.4 months. No acute grade 3 toxicities occurred. Two patients (3.2%) had late grade 3 toxicity. QoL changes did not meet criteria for a minimal clinically important difference. Three-year survival rates were 62.7% (bPFS), 67.5% (rPFS), 73.0% (LRFS), and 85.9% (MFS); there were no differences between fractionation groups (all P > .05). Among 31 patients with GC results, higher scores were associated with worse bPFS, rPFS, LRFS, and MFS. All patients with GC score >0.85 (n = 4) experienced biochemical, local, and metastatic recurrence. Conclusion DE-fsHDR is a safe and effective salvage treatment for IPR. GC score is a promising prognostic tool in patients undergoing salvage local therapy for IPR and warrants further study to guide treatment intensification.

title: Development and Validation of a Human Cadaveric Model for Lobar Intracerebral Hemorrhage.
abstract: Background and objectives To develop and validate an anatomically accurate human cadaveric intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) model that replicates the radiographic and mechanical properties of spontaneous lobar ICH, enabling training and testing of minimally invasive surgical evacuation techniques. Methods Human-derived thrombi were created using mixtures of banked human packed red blood cells, fresh-frozen plasma, and iodinated contrast. Thrombi with physiologic viscoelastic properties were identified through rheometric analysis benchmarked against patient-derived intraoperative ICH specimens. Fresh, never-frozen cadaveric head-and-neck specimens were obtained via the institutional willed body program. After partial embalming, transorbital surgical corridors enabled clot placement in the frontal, temporal, and parietal lobes, while an infratentorial midline mini-craniotomy was used to insert occipital lobe clots. Results Human-derived clots composed of 95% fresh-frozen plasma most closely mimicked the mechanical properties of real ICH specimens. Transorbital and occipital approaches allowed for precise, reproducible hematoma placement. Flat-panel computed tomography imaging provided sufficient radiodensity contrast to delineate the clot from the surrounding brain parenchyma. Conclusion We report the first human cadaveric lobar ICH model using rheologically validated, surgically implanted human-derived clots. This model provides a reproducible platform for device evaluation, procedural development, and training in minimally invasive surgical evacuation of ICH.

title: Hybrid Molecular Imaging Using PET/CT and PET/MRI in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: Current Applications, Challenges, and Future Perspectives.
abstract: Hybrid molecular imaging is increasingly recognized as a valuable tool for the precision management of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Driven by the treat-to-target paradigm, the noninvasive quantification of transmural inflammation and the accurate differentiation of stricture phenotypes remain key clinical challenges. Current evidence indicates that although 2-deoxy-2-¹⁸F-fluoro-D-glucose (¹⁸F-FDG) positron emission tomography (PET) can effectively quantify the overall inflammatory burden, the integration of fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (FAPI)-targeted PET imaging provides important complementary value for characterizing fibro-inflammatory remodeling and distinguishing fibrotic strictures. By combining high metabolic sensitivity with high-resolution multiparametric soft-tissue characterization, PET/magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has demonstrated potential advantages in assessing penetrating complications and facilitating longitudinal therapeutic monitoring. Pediatric and young adult patients requiring long-term follow-up may derive substantial benefit from the reduced radiation exposure offered by integrated PET/MRI systems. To overcome conventional method limitations, including physiologic intestinal uptake and attenuation-correction artifacts, the field is actively exploring novel molecularly targeted tracers, ultra-low-dose long-axial-field-of-view whole-body systems, and artificial intelligence-based image reconstruction techniques. Given that substantial current evidence is derived from small, single-center cohorts and experimental studies, these advanced modalities currently serve as adjunctive, problem-solving tools rather than routine replacements for standard endoscopy or conventional cross-sectional imaging. This review comprehensively evaluates the clinical performance, applicability, and translational barriers of hybrid molecular imaging in IBD, underscoring the urgent need to establish standardized, multicenter consensus protocols that can guide its future implementation in individualized therapeutic strategies.

title: Allostatic load, genetic susceptibility, and lung cancer risk: Evidence from a prospective cohort and integrative proteomic analyses.
abstract: Allostatic load (AL), a composite measure of multisystem dysregulation associated with chronic stress, has been linked to lung cancer risk. However, its joint effects with genetic susceptibility and the biological pathways underlying this relationship remain unclear. We conducted a prospective cohort study of 336,945 UK Biobank participants to assess associations between AL and lung cancer incidence and its histological subtypes. A polygenic risk score was constructed to evaluate the joint associations of AL and genetic susceptibility. We further assessed whether AL provided incremental risk stratification beyond established low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) screening eligibility frameworks and integrated plasma proteomic data using machine learning, enrichment, and mediation analyses. We found that higher AL was associated with an increased risk of lung cancer (per-unit HR = 1.073, 95% CI: 1.053-1.094; Low vs. Normal HR = 1.284, 95% CI: 1.065-1.547; High vs. Normal HR = 1.629, 95% CI: 1.347-1.971). Subtype analyses revealed the strongest effect for small-cell lung cancer (SCLC), with significant associations also observed for lung adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma. High AL combined with high genetic risk was associated with a 136.9% increased risk (HR = 2.369, 95% CI: 1.565-3.583), without evidence of interaction. title: Brain tumor segmentation using a combination of graph cut and optimized U-Net with genetic algorithm: An efficient hybrid framework for enhanced medical image analysis.
abstract: Accurate segmentation of low-grade gliomas (LGGs) in FLAIR MRI remains challenging due to low-contrast tumor boundaries, irregular morphology, and extreme class imbalance. This work presents a lightweight hybrid segmentation framework that integrates three complementary components: (1) a fast graph-based region refinement step using GrabCut applied during training only to enhance tumor-background contrast, (2) a compact U-Net architecture whose filter configuration is automatically selected using a small-scale genetic algorithm, and (3) an analytical evaluation of lightweight post-processing strategies studied separately from the final GA-optimized model. The method was evaluated on the LGG-MRI-Segmentation dataset using strict patient-level splits of 79 training, 19 validation, and 12 testing patients. The final model achieved strong slice-wise performance with a mean Dice of 0.9132 and a median Dice of 0.9855; the lower mean reflects the influence of more difficult, lower-performing slices and therefore provides a more conservative summary of overall performance across the evaluated test cases. Additional metrics include an IoU of 0.8851, sensitivity of 0.8954, precision of 0.9523, specificity of 0.9997, and an HD95 of 1.00 mm, indicating highly accurate boundary delineation. For contextual benchmarking, a 2D nnU-Net model was trained on the same dataset. nnU-Net achieved a mean validation Dice of 0.8450 and a best validation EMA Dice of 0.9134. Because these nnU-Net Dice values were obtained from its validation workflow rather than the exact slice-wise test procedure used for the proposed model, they are presented as contextual reference results rather than strictly matched test-set estimates. The proposed framework required substantially less training time under the evaluated implementations. Taken together, these findings demonstrate that a carefully coordinated combination of preprocessing, lightweight architectural optimization, and efficient post-processing can achieve strong segmentation performance on the evaluated dataset while remaining computationally efficient. These findings suggest that the proposed framework is promising for computationally constrained LGG segmentation workflows. However, broader clinical applicability requires validation on independent external cohorts before generalizability can be established.

title: Real-world before-and-after evaluation of AI support for lung cancer diagnosis at three US lung nodule clinics.
abstract: Background Health systems and payers require evidence that artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled decision support improves care delivery. Integrating AI into lung nodule management pathways may streamline workflows, improve identification and triage of patients with pulmonary nodules, and enable earlier lung cancer diagnosis. Yet real-world evidence of clinical utility remains limited. This study evaluated the impact of implementing commercially available AI software to support the lung nodule and lung cancer care pathway across three US health systems. Materials and methods A real-world before-and-after study compared clinic activity during matched 12.5-month pre-implementation and post-implementation periods at three US lung nodule clinics. Primary outcomes were the number of new patients and the number of patients undergoing at least one invasive procedure. Secondary outcomes were numbers of lung cancers and early-stage (stages I-II) lung cancers, and time from baseline CT to diagnosis. Analyses used Wilcoxon signed-rank and Mann-Whitney U tests, with medians and interquartile ranges (IQRs) reported for continuous measures. Results Across sites, new patients increased from 138 before to 232 after implementation, equivalent to 11.0 to 18.6 patients per month (p = 0.0002), with the median rising from 9 (IQR 7-14) to 16 (IQR 13-21) patients. Monthly patients undergoing at least one invasive procedure increased from 4.9 to 8.0 (p = 0.0085). Monthly cancers increased from 3.0 to 3.8 (p = 0.3242), while monthly early-stage cancers rose from 1.4 to 2.4 (p = 0.125). Median time to diagnosis was 58 days (IQR 33-158) before and 57 days (IQR 27-85) after implementation (p = 0.26), with IQR narrowing from 125 days to 58 days. Conclusion Implementation of the AI-enabled software was associated with significantly increased throughput of lung nodule patients and procedural volume. These results, observed prospectively post-implementation, suggest AI-assisted identification and triage can expand access to timely specialist review.

title: Regional Brain Structural Changes During the Transition from Acute to Chronic Neuropathic Pain: A Longitudinal Study in a Rat Model of Orofacial Pain.
abstract: Brain imaging studies have identified structural alterations in individuals with chronic neuropathic pain, particularly in regions involved in sensory, emotional, and cognitive processing. However, most studies remain cross-sectional, leaving the temporal progression of these changes during pain chronification unclear. This gap is critical, as both neural and non-neural cells undergo dynamic changes during pain chronification. The primary aim of this study was to track longitudinally regional brain volume and density changes before and after induction of orofacial neuropathic pain in male rats, using a chronic constriction injury of the infraorbital nerve (ION-CCI). This model enables assessment of changes in the spinal trigeminal nucleus (SpVn). T2-weighted magnetic resonance imaging scans were acquired 7 d prior to injury and then at +2, +7, +14, and +28 d, in ION-CCI ( n = 11), sham-injured ( n = 6), and naive ( n = 8) groups. Voxel-based and deformation-based morphometry were used to identify early- and late-onset density and volumetric changes, respectively. Early after injury, transient, bidirectional volume and/or density changes in the ipsilateral primary somatosensory cortex (S1), contralateral SpVn, and bilateral dorsomedial periaqueductal gray, ipsilateral retrosplenial and contralateral prelimbic cortices, were observed. In contrast, late-onset changes were more widespread, with volume increases observed bilaterally in the SpVn pars interpolaris (SpVo), in the ipsilateral dorsomedial SpVn (SpVdm), bilateral lateral hypothalamus, and contralateral amygdalo-hippocampal complex, and volume decreases in contralateral retrosplenial, prelimbic, and bilateral S1 cortices. These findings reveal early dynamic reorganization of sensory and sensory-modulatory brain regions, followed by sustained structural alterations across trigeminal brainstem nuclei, limbic-hypothalamic systems, and higher-order cortical networks.

title: Management of Nondiagnostic Thyroid Fine Needle Aspiration Cytology Nodules Based on TI-RADS Risk Assessment.
abstract: Objective The high prevalence of thyroid nodules and the frequent occurrence of nondiagnostic (ND) results on fine-needle aspiration (FNA) necessitates malignancy risk stratification to balance cancer detection while avoiding unnecessary repeat biopsies. This study evaluated malignancy rates and management strategies for nodules with ND cytology, stratified by the American College of Radiology Thyroid Imaging Reporting and Data System (TI-RADS) score. Methods This retrospective study analyzed 342 consecutive patients with initial ND ultrasound-guided (USG) thyroid FNA from a high volume, two-practitioner clinic between January 2019 and June 2024. Data collected from chart review included Bethesda cytopathology classifications, management approaches, and final histopathological diagnosis when available. Results Among 3717 thyroid FNAs performed during the study period, 342 (9.2%) were ND on initial sampling. TI-RADS (TR) distribution for ND nodules was: TR1 9.6%, TR2 9.9%, TR3 28.1%, TR4 45.3%, TR5 7.0%. Initial management comprised repeat FNA in 170 (49.7%) patients, ultrasound (US) surveillance in 101 (29.5%), surgery in 17 (5.0%); 54 (15.8%) patients were lost to follow-up. Of repeat FNAs, 47 (27.6%) remained ND. Among 33 surgical cases, malignancy was identified in 6 (1.8%) index nodules with initial ND cytology. Five malignancies occurred in TR4 nodules and one in a TR5 nodule. Importantly, there were no malignancies among 17 resected TR1-3 nodules. Conclusion For experienced practitioners in a high-volume clinic, ND thyroid FNA cytology carries a low overall observed risk of malignancy (1.8%). TI-RADS scores should be taken into consideration to guide management decisions for ND cytology nodules between repeat FNA, US surveillance, or surgery.

title: Synergistic Therapeutic Effects of Non-Invasive Aesthetic Technologies and Applied Sports Activity in the Management of Localized Adiposity and Cellulite
abstract: Non-invasive aesthetic technologies, such as cryolipolysis (CLL), radiofrequency (RF), and ultrasound cavitation, have become standard therapeutic approaches for the management of localized adiposity and gynoid lipodystrophy (cellulite). While these technologies effectively induce adipocyte apoptosis or lipolysis, the subsequent clearance of cellular debris and free fatty acids (FFAs) heavily relies on the body’s lymphatic and metabolic pathways. This article explores the therapeutic synergy between applied physical activity and non-invasive body contouring. We hypothesize that integrating targeted exercise—specifically aerobic training and targeted muscle contractions—may act as a therapeutic adjunct to aesthetic sections. Physiologically, exercise-induced muscle pumps accelerate lymphatic drainage, facilitating the rapid removal of metabolic byproducts, while increased energy expenditure promotes the oxidation of released FFAs, preventing their re-esterification. By bridging aesthetic science and applied physical activity, this paper proposes a theoretical framework for combined protocols, intended to guide future clinical investigation and offer a holistic, therapeutic approach to body sculpting.

title: A Rare Presentation of Acute-Onset BCG-Induced Aortic Aneurysm: A Case Report
abstract: Background: Mycotic Aortic aneurysms (MAA) are saccular aneurysms of the infected aortic wall. Mycobacterium, compared with other bacteria, is less likely to cause MAA; most cases follow, but it is a rare, late, systemic, and serious complication of intravesical Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) instillation for bladder cancer. Case Presentation: A 65-year-old male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, diabetes mellitus, diabetic foot ulcer with methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA) bacteremia, status post partial toe amputation, and papillary urothelial carcinoma treated with transurethral resection and intravesical BCG instillation, recently underwent a computed tomography (CT) abdomen 2 weeks ago for abdominal pain, which revealed colonic stool without other pathological findings, who currently presented with worsening abdominal pain, and the CT scan identified a new 2.5-centimeter pseudoaneurysm of the infrarenal aorta, associated with a periaortic and aortocaval mass, likely a hematoma, infectious mycotic aneurysm, or neoplastic process. The patient received intravenous piperacillin-tazobactam for presumed MSSA, a potential cause of a mycotic aneurysm, which was later discontinued after negative blood cultures. Vascular surgery consultation led to endovascular aortic stenting. Infectious disease recommended a Karius test; despite no warning signs, it returned positive for the Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex, and a diagnosis of a BCG-induced aneurysm was made. title: Pulmonary Alveolar Microlithiasis: From Clinicopathologic Description to Molecular Pathogenesis and Emerging Therapies
abstract: Pulmonary alveolar microlithiasis (PAM) is a rare autosomal recessive lung disease in which calcium phosphate microliths fill the alveoli. Although the cause of it remained unknown for some time, more recently loss-of-function variants in SLC34A2, which encodes the sodium-phosphate cotransporter NPT2b, explain nearly all genetically tested cases; failure to clear phosphate from the alveolar lining fluid leads to microlith formation, and an epithelial Npt2b-knockout mouse reproduces the human phenotype. Diagnosis now rests mainly on characteristic high-resolution CT and, increasingly, on genotyping rather than lung biopsy. The protracted course has been described in some series of cases, with death from respiratory failure. No drug has proven efficacy; lung transplantation is the only established therapy, and no allograft recurrence has been documented. Preclinical data support phosphate restriction, EDTA lavage and gene-directed approaches. However, controlled trials with more genotype-phenotype correlation and prospective natural-history data are still needed.

title: Gastric Fungal Colonization as a Candidate Mechanism in ALS-Spectrum Motor Neuron Disease: A Hypothesis Supported by Five Years of Case Documentation
abstract: Background: The etiology of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) remains unknown in approximately 90% of cases [1]. A unified mechanism linking environmental mycotoxin exposure, gut-brain axis dysfunction, and motor neuron disease has not been systematically investigated. Hypothesis. Chronic colonization of the gastric mucosa by a mycotoxin-producing mold, concealed beneath a mucosal biofilm and therefore potentially undetectable by standard endoscopy, is proposed to drive sustained motor-neuron hyperexcitability through three concurrent mechanisms: (1) TLR activation on vagal afferent fibers projecting excitatory signals to brainstem motor nuclei via neural spill-over; (2) cross-reactive immune attack on motor-neuron surface proteins via molecular mimicry; and (3) Dectin-1-mediated neuroinflammation during biofilm disruption. Case. Five-year index case: five positive urinary Trichothecene assays including one after a 32-hour fast (internal source confirmed); six immunological assessments, including five CD25 measurements, showing markedly reduced measured T-cell activation markers and cytokine responses (CD25 1.0–3.1%, reference 13–24%; IFN-γ 79.5 pg/ml, reference ≥118; IL-17 5.4 pg/ml, reference ≥9.6); EMG-confirmed neurogenic remodeling followed by documented stabilization; over 30 reproducible pharmacological observations consistent with the proposed mechanism; and formal diagnostic exclusion across four institutions over three years. Implications. Convergent findings from the published literature, together with more than 30 internally consistent pharmacological observations, support formal investigation of the proposed model. Proposed initial investigations include urinary mycotoxin testing, lymphocyte transformation testing, mycotoxin antibody testing, visual contrast sensitivity screening, and biofilm-directed endoscopy with confocal laser endomicroscopy, targeted biopsy, and PCR analysis.

title: Biologically Inspired Selective Attention for Prostate MRI: A Segmentation-Guided Vision Transformer Framework for Computer-Aided Diagnosis
abstract: Prostate cancer is the second most commonly diagnosed malignancy in men, yet interpretation of multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) suffers from substantial inter-observer variability and depends on scarce expert radiologists. Expert readers follow a hierarchical, coarse-to-fine visual strategy: they first localize the prostate gland and then direct focused attention to tissue within it. Inspired by this biological selective-attention mechanism, we propose a segmentation-guided framework in which a modality-aware 3D Vision Transformer (ViT) first delineates the prostate gland from T2-weighted, ADC, and DWI volumes, and the resulting anatomical mask then constrains downstream cancer detection. Global self-attention models long-range anatomical context, analogous to the integration of peripheral and foveal information in human vision. Detection was evaluated through two pathways: gray-level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM) texture features with classical classifiers, and a ViT classifier. On 200 patients from the public PROSTATEx cohort, the proposed segmentation model achieved a Dice similarity coefficient of [0.905] versus [0.831] for an optimized U-Net. The segmentation-guided ViT achieved an AUC of [0.987] and an accuracy of [0.998] for clinically significant cancer detection. Ablation experiments confirmed that anatomical guidance improved both pathways. These results show that emulating expert visual search strategies yields accurate and interpretable computer-aided prostate cancer diagnosis.

title: DeepSUM-DWI: A Joint Image Registration and Super-Resolution Convolutional Neural Network for Diffusion-Weighted MRI
abstract: Background: Diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) is an important MRI technique for studying tissue microstructure and structural connectivity, but is limited by relatively low spatial resolution, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and sensitivity to inter-acquisition motion. A deep-learning framework was developed that jointly performs image registration and super-resolution on repeated low-resolution DWI inputs to generate a single registered, higher apparent spatial-resolution output. Methods: DeepSUM-DWI adapts a DeepSUM multi-image super-resolution architecture for repeated DWI. It comprises a shared 2D super-resolution feature extractor (SISRNet), a registration network (RegNet), and a 3D fusion network (FusionNet). Evaluation used (1) simulated repetitions with synthetic motion, (2) retrospectively downsampled acquisitions from 12 subjects, and (3) a prospective dual-resolution example with matched 1.0 × 1.0 and 2.0 × 2.0 mm² acquisitions. Results: DeepSUM-DWI reconstructed a single high-resolution-appearing DWI image from multiple low-resolution repetitions while preserving structural characteristics of the high-resolution acquisitions. The model remained robust across synthetic motion magnitudes. In retrospectively downsampled data, it improved NRMSE by 71–79% and PSNR by 10.6–13.5 dB, for super-resolution factors of 2–3, relative to averaging interpolated low-resolution images, with a mean SSIM > 0.99. In prospectively acquired data, it recovered finer structures than visible in the acquired low-resolution images while maintaining contrast consistency. Exploratory diffusion analysis suggested that some gains in apparent detail propagated to FA maps. Conclusions: DeepSUM-DWI provides a framework for joint registration and super-resolution of repeated DWI acquisitions, with potential to improve apparent spatial resolution while retaining the SNR benefits of repeated acquisition.

title: MRI-Based Radiomics and Machine Learning for Predicting Refractory Outcomes in Ménière’s Disease: A Multicenter Preliminary Study
abstract: Abstract Objective To evaluate the value of a machine learning model based on radiomics features derived from multicenter gadolinium-enhanced inner ear magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for predicting refractory clinical outcomes in patients with Ménière’s disease (MD). Methods This retrospective study enrolled patients with unilateral Ménière’s disease diagnosed at two medical centers between January 2019 and December 2023. A total of 154 patients from Center 1 constituted the internal dataset and were divided into a training set (n = 123) and an internal test set (n = 31) at an 8:2 ratio, while 32 patients from Center 2 were included as an independent external validation set. According to established clinical guidelines, patients were categorized into good-control and poor-control groups. Radiomics features were extracted from the cochlea and vestibule on gadolinium-enhanced 3D-FLAIR-CUBE images, and bilateral difference (Diff) features were generated by subtracting contralateral ear features from those of the affected ear. Feature selection was performed using correlation filtering and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Multiple machine learning algorithms were used to construct predictive models, which were evaluated in both internal and external datasets. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and F1 score, and clinical utility was evaluated using decision curve analysis (DCA). Results In both the training and internal test sets, the Diff radiomics model achieved higher AUCs than the symptomatic-ear radiomics models (training set: 0.815 vs. 0.682; internal test set: 0.730 vs. 0.650), along with improved sensitivity and F1 scores. Feature importance analysis indicated that vestibular-related radiomics features contributed more prominently to the prediction of refractory outcomes. Although model performance declined in the external validation set, the Diff model maintained high sensitivity (0.957) and F1 score. DCA demonstrated greater clinical net benefit of the Diff model in the training and internal test sets. Conclusion A machine learning model based on bilateral difference radiomics features can effectively predict refractory outcomes in MD and demonstrates superior performance compared with single-ear radiomics models. This approach may provide objective imaging support for prognostic assessment and individualized management of patients with MD.

title: Machine-Learning Models Using Multidimensional Habitats MRI Features for Assessing Recurrence and Metastasis Risk in Locally Advanced Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma
abstract: Abstract Background Approximately 30%–40% of patients with locally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma (LANPC) develop local recurrence or distant metastasis. Early identification of high-risk patients is therefore important for improving prognosis. Methods A total of 1,285 patients with LANPC from three medical centers were enrolled. Patients from center A were randomly divided into a training set (n = 693) and a validation set (n = 297) at a ratio of 7:3, while patients from centers B and C were combined as an external test set (n = 295). Ten independent machine learning models and 26 stacked ensemble models were developed. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, and F1 score. The incremental value of multidimensional habitat (MH) features over clinical features alone was assessed using integrated discrimination improvement (IDI), net reclassification improvement (NRI), calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). The SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) method was used to interpret the final model. Results After recursive feature elimination (RFE), four selected clinical features, namely N category, treatment, platelet count (PLT), and smoking status, were identified and further combined with two imaging features, namely multidimensional habitats derived from contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging (T1C MH) and multidimensional habitats derived from T2-weighted imaging (T2WI MH), for model development. The stacked ensemble model combining support vector machine (SVM), gradient boosting machine (GBM), and logistic regression (LR) achieved the best overall performance, with a mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.761 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.719–0.798) in the 5-fold cross-validation set, 0.742 (95% CI: 0.679–0.801) in the validation set, and 0.721 (95% CI: 0.660–0.776) in the external test set. Conclusion In conclusion, the stacking model constructed based on SVM, GBM, and LR, integrating MH features and clinical features, demonstrated favorable predictive performance for recurrence and metastasis in LANPC patients, and holds promise as an effective tool for individualized risk assessment. Evidence Level: 3 Technical Efficacy: Stage 2

title: Early-onset adenocarcinoma of the ampullary rectum: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background : Early-onset colorectal cancer can present with nonspecific gastrointestinal symptoms, contributing to delayed diagnosis. Adenocarcinoma arising in the ampullary region of the rectum may pose additional diagnostic and surgical challenges because of its distal location. Case presentation : A 33-year-old man presented with nonspecific gastrointestinal complaints. Colonoscopy demonstrated an exophytic tumor involving the lower and middle ampullary regions of the rectum, with luminal narrowing and contact bleeding. Computed tomography showed rectal wall thickening and mesorectal lymph nodes. Histopathological examination confirmed poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma (G3) with lymphovascular and perineural invasion. The final pathological stage was pT3N0M0, with no metastatic lymph nodes identified. The patient underwent abdominoperineal excision of the rectum with sigmoid colon pull-through and had an uncomplicated early postoperative course. Conclusions : This case emphasizes the need to consider colorectal malignancy in younger adults with persistent or unexplained gastrointestinal symptoms. Prompt endoscopic assessment and histopathological confirmation are essential when symptoms are atypical or persistent. Histological risk features should be integrated with tumor stage when planning postoperative management.

title: New-Onset Continuous Urinary Incontinence After Ectopic Ureteral Stone Surgery with Pre-existing Stress Urinary Incontinence: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background: Adult ectopic ureter is uncommon and may be overlooked when a common cause of urinary incontinence coexists. Case presentation: A 66-year-old woman had a 2-year history of intermittent urinary leakage during coughing or physical activity. She later developed right flank pain and fever. Computed tomography (CT) demonstrated bilateral duplicated collecting systems and a right upper-pole ectopic ureter opening into the urethra, with an approximately 11×8 mm calculus impacted near its distal opening (Fig. 1A, B). Ureteroscopic lithotripsy relieved the flank pain. Subsequent urodynamic evaluation demonstrated moderate stress urinary incontinence (SUI) (Fig. 1C), and a tension-free vaginal tape (TVT) procedure initially improved the leakage. One month after TVT, however, the leakage changed to continuous urine loss unrelated to coughing, activity, or body position. Repeat urodynamics were normal, and the leaking fluid remained clear during bladder methylene blue instillation. Cystoscopic reassessment and review of the known duplicated anatomy raised suspicion of an ectopic urinary source (Fig. 2A). Laparoscopy confirmed the ectopic right upper-pole ureter (Fig. 2B), which was reimplanted into the bladder. Postoperative retrograde pyelography documented the reconstructed system (Fig. 2C), and the patient no longer experienced urinary leakage. Conclusion: This case illustrates that ectopic ureter may be easily missed when coexisting SUI provides a convincing explanation for urinary leakage. A transition from stress-related intermittent leakage to continuous, position-independent leakage should trigger reassessment of the diagnosis. In patients with a duplicated collecting system, integration of symptom phenotype, urodynamics, dye testing, cystoscopy, and cross-sectional imaging can help identify an ectopic urinary source and avoid diagnostic delay.

title: Clinical analysis of mycosis fungoides involving the central nervous system：a case report
abstract: Abstract Background Mycosis fungoides (MF) with central nervous system (CNS) involvement is a rare complication of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma(CTCL) without unified diagnostic and therapeutic criteria.We retrospectively analyzed the clinical presentation, diagnostic and therapeutic course, and prognosis of a single case of MF with CNS involvement treated at our institution.Combined neuroimaging, cerebrospinal fluid flow cytometry suggested CNS infiltration, and stereotactic biopsy, histopathology together with positive T-cell receptor gene rearrangement confirmed the diagnosis.This case indicates high vigilance for CNS dissemination in MF patients with new neurological symptoms. It highlights that CNS involvement should be suspected in MF patients with new neurological symptoms, and combined imaging, cerebrospinal fluid testing and biopsy enables timely diagnosis of CNS dissemination in advanced MF. Case Presentation: We report a 49-year-old male with mycosis fungoides (MF) who developed new-onset left facial hypesthesia and left upper limb weakness. Neuroimaging revealed a right frontal lobe lesion with multiple extracranial hypermetabolic foci. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed aberrant T-lymphocytes, supporting a diagnosis of MF with central nervous system (CNS) involvement. The patient initially responded to systemic chemotherapy but was subsequently complicated by septic shock and hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis. Two months later, follow-up imaging showed new brain lesions; stereotactic biopsy and positive T-cell receptor gene rearrangement confirmed persistent CNS involvement. Conclusions This case highlights that in MF patients presenting with CNS symptoms,the diagnosis of MF with CNS involvement should be considered and an aggressive diagnostic workup, including imageological assessment, lumbar puncture, tissue biopsy and so on, should be pursued to establish a diagnosis. Therapeutic strategies must be individualized based on each patient's specific disease status.

title: Utility of intravoxel incoherent motion diffusion-weighted imaging in predicting pathological response to neoadjuvant immuno-chemotherapy for locally advanced gastric cancer
abstract: Abstract Background To investigate the feasibility of intravoxel incoherent motion diffusion-weighted imaging (IVIM) for predicting pathological tumor regression grade (TRG) after neoadjuvant immuno-chemotherapy (NICT) in locally advanced gastric cancer (LAGC). Methods Between January 2022 and December 2024, consecutive patients with endoscopy-biopsy confirmed gastric adenocarcinoma undergoing NICT followed by curative gastrectomy were prospectively recruited. Stomach MRI examinations, including IVIM, were performed within one week before NICT initiation. Patients were classified as responders (TRG 0/1) or non-responders (TRG 2/3). The apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC), IVIM-derived true diffusion coefficient (D), pseudodiffusion coefficient (D*), and pseudodiffusion fraction ( f ) were measured and compared between the two groups. Independent predictors of non-responders were identified and used to establish a combined parameter. The performances of IVIM-derived parameters were assessed using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis. The relationship between the combined parameter and patient survival outcomes was explored using Kaplan–Meier survival analysis. Results Ninety-three patients (74 males, 19 females; mean age 59.0 ± 9.9 years) were finally recruited. ADC and D were significantly lower, whereas f was higher in non-responders compared with those in responders ( p < 0.05). ADC, D, and f were independent predictors of non-responders. Their combination outperformed each individual parameter, achieving an area under the curve of 0.779, and was associated with patient disease-free survival (DFS) (hazard ratio = 3.624). Conclusion IVIM is feasible for early prediction of treatment response to the emerging NICT in LAGC; ADC, D, and f are equally useful and their combination demonstrated incremental benefit and prognostic value for patient DFS.

title: A Rare Combined Hematoma of the Retzius Space and Broad Ligament Complicating Short Second-Stage Labor: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background Postpartum pelvic hematoma is an uncommon but life-threatening obstetric complication following vaginal delivery. Isolated broad ligament hematomas are occasionally reported, while hematomas confined to the Retzius space are extremely rare. Concurrent composite hematoma involving both anatomical compartments after short second-stage labor represents a scarcely reported clinical entity. This concealed hemorrhagic condition presents with non-specific symptoms, often leading to delayed diagnosis and increased maternal morbidity. Case presentation : A 33-year-old gravida 2, para 1 woman achieved vaginal delivery at 38 weeks of gestation with a short second-stage labor of 27 minutes. Three hours postpartum, the patient developed persistent suprapubic pain and urinary retention without remarkable external vaginal bleeding. Physical examination revealed hypotension, suprapubic tenderness, and tense anterior vaginal fornix. Laboratory tests showed a marked hemoglobin decline from 116 g/L to 85 g/L. Pelvic ultrasound identified a large 14.4 × 9.2 × 9.0 cm Retzius space hematoma. Considering progressive anemia and hemodynamic instability, emergency exploratory laparotomy was performed. Intraoperative findings confirmed synchronous hematomas in the Retzius space and right broad ligament. A bleeding point beneath the infundibulopelvic ligament was identified and ligated. The broad ligament peritoneum was closed with interrupted sutures. The patient had an uneventful postoperative course and was discharged on postoperative day 5. Conclusions Combined Retzius space and broad ligament hematoma is a rare concealed postpartum emergency strongly associated with precipitous labor. Atypical urinary symptoms without obvious vaginal bleeding easily led to misdiagnosis. Venous-origin diffuse bleeding limits the efficacy of arterial embolization. For large multi-compartment hematomas with compressive symptoms, open laparotomy enables thorough hemostasis and resolves pelvic mass effects effectively. Early clinical suspicion and timely surgical intervention are critical for favorable maternal outcomes.
